mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 5% over two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, which raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when FEDFUNDS exceeds 5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a drop in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 10% month-over-month indicates weakening consumer demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes under these conditions.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 4.5% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate hiring, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly below zero (t-test p > 0.10) during such periods.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% for four consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces earnings visibility for S&P 500 constituents and leads to negative returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO MoM < -1% for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 35% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of more than 300,000 in a single month, combined with a concurrent decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.4 percentage points, signals a tight labor market that increases wage pressures and inflation risk, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly above zero (t-test p > 0.05) in triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) of more than 5% signals a shift from consumption to saving, which typically precedes a slowdown in demand and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid decline in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 2% while the federal funds rate remains above 5% for three months signals a policy lag and potential easing expectation, which supports equity valuations and produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL < 102 AND FEDFUNDS > 5.0% for three months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly above zero (t-test p > 0.10) in triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A consistent monthly increase in housing starts (HOUST) of more than 5% for three consecutive months signals a recovery in residential construction demand, which boosts materials and homebuilder sector earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST MoM > 5% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly above zero (t-test p > 0.05) in triggered episodes.
